properties.statement:
THE GIT MERGE DRIVER AND `export_graph` SERIALIZE THE SAME DESIGN IN DIFFERENT KEY ORDERS, SO THE FIRST CANONICAL EXPORT AFTER ANY MERGE REWRITES THE WHOLE FILE. Found by doing it, 2026-08-15, on a PR that had to rebase twice because three other PRs landed while it was open.

MEASURED. After `git rebase origin/main` resolved `docs/design/reflow2.json` through reflow2's own merge driver ('merged 2251 node(s) and 8845 edge(s) — 56 divergence(s) resolved automatically, no conflicts'), that merged file was committed and reached main. Its first key is `stamp`. A fresh `export_graph` of the same design writes `content_hash` first, then `edges`, then the rest — alphabetical. `git diff --stat` between them: **60,793 insertions and 60,134 deletions on a ~90,000-line file**, with every node id appearing as added. The CONTENT is identical where it should be; only the serialization order differs.

WHY IT MATTERS, and it is the tool's own stated contract: `export_graph`'s description says the document is 'sorted so two exports of an unchanged graph are byte-identical', and the `path` parameter promises 'deterministic sorted-key JSON, diffable under git'. That property is what makes a design export reviewable in a pull request at all. The merge driver silently opts a repository out of it, and nothing reports that it has happened — the file is valid, the gate is green, the lineage chain is correct, and the diff is unreadable.

THE COMPOUNDING PART: a reviewer looking at a 60k-line diff cannot see the fifteen nodes the PR actually added. A real regression in that diff would be invisible for exactly the same reason. And it is self-perpetuating in the other direction too — whichever form lands on main, the next contributor's tool writes the other one.

SEPARATELY AND MORE SERIOUSLY, FOUND IN THE SAME MINUTE: THE MERGE DRIVER UPDATES THE FILE AND NOT THE STORE, so the next export from that seat REGRESSES whatever the merge resolved. Measured: after the rebase, `art:adopt-skill`, `art:graph` and `art:skill-lint` carried NEWER checksums in the merged file (matching the files on disk) than in the live graph, which had never seen them. Exporting from that store rolled all three back to stale digests and the gate correctly reported three `checksum_change` drifts — on a working tree this session had not touched. Main was green; only the export was wrong. THE REMEDY IS `import_graph` ON THE COMMITTED EXPORT BEFORE EXPORTING, which is what `sync_status` says in ordinary language and what nothing says after a merge, because the merge leaves the seat looking `in_step`: the recorded hash is compared against the FILE, and the file is exactly where this seat left it — it was the STORE that fell behind.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: both orderings observed on one repository, one day; the regression reproduced and then fixed by importing before exporting; the gate caught it. WHAT IS NOT: whether the merge driver's order is stable across runs, whether any other property is dropped or reordered besides key order, and how many past PRs merged a non-canonical export without anyone noticing (cheap to sweep by checking each commit's first key, not yet done).

FIX SHAPES: have the merge driver emit the canonical form (the exporter's serializer, not its own), which removes both symptoms at once for the file; and, for the store half, either write the merge result back through the graph or make the post-merge state visible so `in_step` cannot be read as `up to date`.
